source.title: Some Results and Open Problems on the Controllability of Linear and Semilinear Heat Equations

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a bounded smooth domain, let ω be a nonempty open subset of Ω, and consider the linear heat equation φ_t − Δφ = 0 in Ω × (0,T) with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions on ∂Ω × (0,T). There exist constants γ > 0 and C > 0 such that the weighted observability inequality ∫_0^T∫_Ω e^{-γ/t} φ(x,t)^2 dx dt ≤ C ∫_0^T∫_ω φ(x,t)^2 dx dt holds for every solution, and the analogous inequality also makes sense on the infinite time interval because the L²-norm of solutions decays exponentially. Determine the best possible constant γ in these observability inequalities, in particular in the infinite-time version ∫_0^∞∫_Ω e^{-γ/t} φ(x,t)^2 dx dt ≤ C ∫_0^∞∫_ω φ(x,t)^2 dx dt, and decide whether the lower bound γ ≥ sup_{B(x_0,p)⊂Ω\ω} p^2/4 is sharp, especially in radially symmetric geometries.
accepted.context_brief: Sharp observability constants for the constant-coefficient heat equation

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a bounded smooth domain, let ω be a nonempty open subset of Ω, and consider the heat equation with bounded potential φ_t − Δφ + a(x,t)φ = 0 in Ω × (0,T) with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions, where a ∈ L^∞(Ω × (0,T)). Existing observability estimates involve a factor of the form exp(C‖a‖_∞^{2/3}). Determine whether one can improve this dependence to exp(C‖a‖_∞^{1/2}), or otherwise obtain a sharper observability inequality with weaker growth in ‖a‖_∞, for example by proving suitable Carleman inequalities in spaces of the form L^p(0,T;L^q(Ω)) rather than only in L²(Ω × (0,T)).
accepted.context_brief: Observability for heat equations with bounded potential

evidence.quote: This suggests that the factor exp ( C || a ||~3) could possibly be replaced by exp(C || a ||~2).

One could think of Carleman inequalities in spaces L P (O, T; Lq(O)). This could lead to an improvement of the factor exp (C || a ||~3) and consequently to a relaxation of the growth condition on the nonlinearity ensuring null-controllability.

accepted.question_text: Consider the semilinear heat equation u_t − Δu + f(u) = v1_ω in a bounded smooth domain Ω, with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions on ∂Ω × (0,T), control region ω ⊂ Ω open and nonempty, and a locally Lipschitz nonlinearity f satisfying f(0)=0 together with the local well-posedness assumptions used in the chapter. The chapter proves null-controllability when f grows strictly slower than |s|(log|s|)^{3/2} at infinity and gives counterexamples when f grows like |s|(log|s|)^p with p>2. Determine whether the system is null-controllable in the intermediate range C_1|s|(log|s|)^{3/2} ≤ |f(s)| ≤ C_2|s|(log|s|)^2 as |s|→∞, or more generally relax the known sufficient growth conditions for null-controllability, especially for nonlinearities growing slower than |s|(log|s|)^2 or such that 1/√|F(s)| is not integrable at infinity, where F(s)=∫_0^s f(σ)dσ.
accepted.context_brief: Growth thresholds for null-controllability of semilinear heat equations

accepted.question_text: For the heat equation on an unbounded conical domain Ω, with control acting on the boundary or on a bounded region as in the half-line and half-space problems discussed in the chapter, decide whether the negative null-controllability result proved for the half-line and extended to the half-space remains true in every conical domain. The main obstacle identified in the chapter is that, although similarity variables still apply in conical domains, the existing method does not extend because the traces of the normal derivatives of the relevant eigenfunctions on ∂Ω are not orthogonal.
accepted.context_brief: Failure of null-controllability on general conical domains

evidence.quote: On the other hand, the similarity variables apply in any conical domain O. However, the methods in [23] do not apply in such a general geometric setting because of the lack of orthogonality of the traces of the normal derivatives of the eigenfunctions on 80.
It would be interesting to know if the negative result of Section 3, extended to R~ in [23}, holds in any conical domain.

accepted.question_text: Consider the one-dimensional variable-coefficient heat equation on the half-line p(x)u_t − (a(x)u_x)_x = 0 for x>0 and t>0, with boundary control u(0,t)=v(t) and initial datum u(x,0)=u_0(x), where a and p are positive, bounded, smooth functions. Determine whether the lack of null-controllability proved in the chapter for the constant-coefficient half-line heat equation extends to this more general variable-coefficient setting. More generally, determine whether the same negative phenomenon persists for equations whose coefficients depend on both x and t, for equations with lower-order potentials, or for semilinear variants on the half-line.
accepted.context_brief: Variable-coefficient and semilinear half-line heat equations

evidence.quote: It would be interesting to see if the negative results of Section 3 may be extended to this more general equation (with, say, a and p positive, bounded and smooth functions).
Of course, the same problem arises for more general equations: coefficients depending both on x and t, equations with lower order potentials, equations involving semilinear terms, ....
